name: apt
summary: Search, install, upgrade and remove software on Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives.

install.note: Only on Debian-family systems. Yocto/Buildroot images normally have no package manager: software is added to the image recipe at build time (e.g. IMAGE_INSTALL in Yocto).

compat: apt is meant for interactive use; scripts traditionally use apt-get. Package names differ between distributions.

examples.title: Search for a package
examples.explain: Searches names and descriptions in the local package lists. Does not need root.

examples.title: Show details about a package
examples.explain: Version, size, dependencies and description. Check this before installing.

examples.title: Refresh the package lists
examples.explain: Downloads the latest lists of available packages. Changes nothing installed. 'Unable to locate package' often just means you forgot this step.
examples.warning: Needs root and network access. Only reads remote lists; installed software is unchanged.

examples.title: Install a package
examples.explain: Shows the packages that will be installed and asks for confirmation. Read that list before answering Y. For C development the usual starting point is build-essential.
examples.warning: Installs software system-wide as root. Only install packages from repositories you trust.

examples.title: Upgrade installed packages
examples.explain: Installs newer versions of what you already have, after sudo apt update.
examples.warning: Changes many system packages at once and may restart services. Avoid in the middle of important work; read the summary before confirming.

examples.title: Remove a package
examples.explain: Removes the package but keeps its system-wide configuration files (purge removes those too).
examples.warning: apt may also remove packages that depend on this one. Read the list it prints; if it contains things like your desktop or network manager, answer n.

name: dpkg
summary: Low-level Debian package tool: which package owns a file, and what files a package installed.

install.note: Debian-family only. On RPM systems the equivalent is rpm -qf <file> and rpm -ql <package>; on Arch pacman -Qo and pacman -Ql.

compat: dpkg -S only finds files of installed packages. To search packages you have not installed, use apt-file (package apt-file).

examples.title: Which installed package provides this file?
examples.explain: For example, dpkg -S /usr/bin/readelf answers binutils-... packages.
options: Search installed packages for a file path

examples.title: List files installed by a package
examples.explain: Shows where headers, libraries and binaries ended up, e.g. dpkg -L libusb-1.0-0-dev.
options: List files of an installed package

examples.title: Is a package installed, and which version?
examples.explain: Lines starting with ii are installed. Quote patterns containing *.

name: dnf
summary: Search, install, upgrade and remove software on Fedora, RHEL, CentOS Stream and similar.

install.note: Only on Fedora/RHEL-family systems. Older releases use yum with mostly the same sub-commands.

compat: Package names often differ from Debian: e.g. development headers end in -devel instead of -dev.

examples.title: Search for a package
examples.explain: Searches names and summaries. May download fresh metadata first.

examples.title: Find which package provides a file
examples.explain: Works for files of packages you have not installed yet, e.g. a missing header.

examples.title: Install a package
examples.explain: Prints the transaction summary and asks for confirmation. For C development, a common start is sudo dnf install gcc make.
examples.warning: Installs software system-wide as root. Read the transaction summary before confirming.

examples.title: Upgrade the system
examples.explain: Refreshes metadata and upgrades all installed packages.
examples.warning: Changes many packages at once; a kernel update needs a reboot to take effect.

name: pacman
summary: Arch Linux package manager: sync, search, install and query packages.
compat: Arch does not support partial upgrades: do not run pacman -Sy <package> alone; upgrade the whole system with -Syu, then install.

examples.title: Which package owns a file?
examples.explain: -Q queries the local database of installed packages; -o asks for the owner of a file.

examples.title: Upgrade everything, then install
examples.explain: -y refreshes package lists, -u upgrades all packages, then <package> is installed, keeping the system consistent.
examples.warning: Performs a full system upgrade as root. Read the package list before confirming and check the Arch news for manual steps.

name: apk
summary: Alpine Linux package manager, common in containers and small systems.

install.note: Only on Alpine. Alpine uses musl libc and BusyBox, so some GNU options and glibc-built binaries behave differently.

compat: Commands below need root: in containers you often already are root; otherwise prefix doas or sudo.

examples.title: Search for a package
examples.explain: Searches the package index. Run apk update first if results look stale.

examples.title: Install packages
examples.explain: Installs the package and its dependencies. For C development: apk add build-base.
examples.warning: Must run as root and changes the system. In a Dockerfile, prefer apk add --no-cache to keep images small.

examples.title: Remove a package
examples.explain: Removes the package and dependencies nothing else needs.
examples.warning: Removes software as root. Check what else depends on it before removing.
